title: The books: Torah, Gospel, Qur'an
hook: There's a Bible on your family's shelf and a Qur'an on yours. Here's how Muslims see both.

screens.text: Believing in Allah's books is the third article of faith [Q 2:285], and the one that comes up most with Christian family. Today: which books, what Muslims believe about the Bible, and how the Qur'an was kept, word for word, for fourteen centuries.
**Allah has always sent guidance.** The Qur'an names four books, each given to a prophet.
bubbles: The **Tawrah** (Torah), given to **Musa** (Moses), and the **Zabur** (Psalms), given to **Dawud** (David) [Q 4:163].
The **Injil** (Gospel), given to **Isa** (Jesus), full of guidance and light [Q 5:46]. And the **Qur'an**, given to Muhammad ﷺ [Q 3:3].
It also mentions the scriptures of Ibrahim (Abraham) and Musa [Q 87:18–19].

screens.prompt: Match each book to the prophet who received it.

screens.title: What Muslims believe about the Bible

cards.front: Do Muslims respect the Torah and the Gospel?
cards.back: Yes. Muslims believe the original Torah and Gospel came from Allah, with guidance and light [Q 5:46]. Believing in them is part of your faith.

cards.front: Is today's Bible the same as what Jesus received?
cards.back: Muslims believe much truth remains in it, but over centuries parts were lost or changed by people [Revealed Path ch. 10]. That's why we don't treat it as the final word.
It's the last message, for everyone. It confirms the truth that came before and acts as the guard over it [Q 5:48].

cards.front: Do I have to argue about which verses are original?
cards.back: No. When Jews read their scripture to the Companions, the Prophet ﷺ told them neither to accept nor reject it, but to say: we believe in Allah and what He revealed [Bukhari 4485; Q 2:136].

events.title: Revealed, memorized, written
events.text: The Qur'an came over 23 years. While the Prophet ﷺ was alive, Companions learned it by heart and wrote it down.

events.title: One complete copy
events.text: The caliph Abu Bakr had Zayd ibn Thabit, one of the Prophet's ﷺ scribes, gather every written piece into one copy [Bukhari 4986].

events.title: Copies for every region
events.text: Later, the caliph Uthman had copies made from it and sent one to each region [Bukhari 4987].

events.title: Kept by heart
events.text: Almost every Muslim community has people, many of them children, who know it all by heart: a **hafiz**. The Arabic is the same in Texas, Senegal and Indonesia.

screens.prompt: Put the Qur'an's journey in order.
items: Memorized and written down in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime
Gathered into one copy under Abu Bakr
Copies sent to each region under Uthman
Known by heart by a hafiz in your city today
screens.feedback: That's the chain: memorized and written from the start, gathered, copied, and still recited by heart [Bukhari 4986; Bukhari 4987].

screens.text: **Allah promised to guard it** [Q 15:9]. Translations differ, which is why Muslims call them "the meaning of the Qur'an," not the Qur'an itself.

screens.prompt: Ana's aunt, a churchgoer, asks quietly: "So you think my Bible is fake?" What's Ana's best answer?

options.text: "No. I believe God really did send the Torah and the Gospel, and I respect them. I believe the Qur'an is His last message, and that's the one I follow."
options.feedback: Yes. Honest, respectful, and it starts with what you share. That's the Muslim position, said kindly.
Not quite. It's not accurate either: Muslims believe much truth remains. And it hurts someone you love for no reason.

options.text: "I don't really know what Muslims think about that."
options.feedback: Not quite. You know more now. Muslims believe the original Torah and Gospel came from God. Lead with that.

steps: One sentence on the Torah and the Gospel
One on the Bible today, one on the Qur'an
Say them to one person, or out loud to yourself
screens.optional_extra: Listen to a short surah you know, like al-Ikhlas, recited by a hafiz online. It's the same Arabic recited everywhere in the world.

screens.text: Muslims believe in the Torah, Psalms and Gospel as Allah's books, and in the Qur'an as His last word, kept unchanged.
You can honor your family's book and still follow yours.

check.prompt: Which book was given to Isa (Jesus)?

options.feedback: Right. The Qur'an says it held guidance and light [Q 5:46].
Not quite. The Zabur was given to Dawud (David). Isa received the Injil.

check.prompt: What do Muslims believe about the original Torah and Gospel?

options.feedback: Right. Believing in Allah's books is an article of faith. The Qur'an is the last of them.
Not quite. Muslims believe the originals were revealed by Allah [Q 3:3; Q 5:46].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Belief in Allah's books is part of iman [Q 2:285]. Named: Tawrah to Musa, Zabur to Dawud [Q 4:163], Injil to Isa [Q 5:46], the Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ [Q 3:3]; also the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa [Q 87:18–19].
- The Qur'an confirms earlier scripture and is a criterion (guard, muhaymin) over it [Q 5:48]. Mainstream belief: the earlier scriptures in their original form came from Allah; much has been lost or altered by people over time [Revealed Path ch. 10].
- When People of the Book relate their scripture, neither confirm nor deny it; say "We believe in Allah and what was revealed to us" [Bukhari 4485; Q 2:136].
- Preservation: memorized and written in the Prophet's lifetime; collected into one copy under Abu Bakr by Zayd ibn Thabit [Bukhari 4986]; Uthman had standard copies made and sent to the provinces [Bukhari 4987]. Allah promised to guard it [Q 15:9]; it's made easy to remember [Q 54:17].

**Likely questions**
- *"Can I read the Bible?"* Many scholars say a Muslim grounded in their own faith can read it for understanding, e.g. to talk with family; a new Muslim should first build their Qur'an reading. Personal decision with the imam; don't rule.
- *"How do we know the Qur'an wasn't changed?"* Mass memorization from the start, writing in the Prophet's lifetime, the Abu Bakr and Uthman compilations, and an unbroken chain of teachers to today. Offer more depth if wanted.
- *"Translation vs. Qur'an?"* The Qur'an is the Arabic; translations convey meaning and are human work. That's why prayer is in Arabic (Q13: never recite a translation in prayer).
- *"Grandma wants to read the Bible with me."* Value the closeness. They might share stories both books honor (Mary, Jesus's birth: Day 27). The convert doesn't have to accept everything read; kind honesty is fine. If it becomes pressure, see Day 35.
- *"Was the Gospel written by Jesus?"* Brief: Muslims believe Allah gave Jesus a revelation (the Injil); the Gospels in the Bible today were written by others after him. Don't debate Christian scholarship.

**Escalate:** detailed polemics (specific Bible passages, textual criticism); requests to debate a pastor or family member.

**Don't**
- Don't call the Bible "fake" or mock it (rule 8). Don't quote Bible verses as proofs.
- Don't make claims about manuscripts beyond the lesson facts.
- Don't bring up verses that rebuke earlier communities for altering scripture; they're for a teacher to explain in context, not for a family conversation.
